methodology.title: How this assessment is produced

steps.how: Ordinary code checks types, ranges and units. Inputs left blank are recorded as not provided; nothing is filled in on your behalf.
Dimension-checked arithmetic on the numbers you supplied, reported with the significant figures of the inputs and with its assumptions. A calculation is skipped when an input is missing.

A fixed set of rules compares your inputs with reference conditions and with provisions the cited literature describes. Each rule's wording is tied to specific statements in a curated source library, or is labelled as inference. Provisions you describe are taken as you describe them and are not checked.

Sources come from a curated list of NASA documents. The library records how much of each was actually read (full text or abstract only). Astroflare can re-check that each record still exists at its publisher; this confirms the record and its title, not its content. Astroflare does not search the literature.
steps.automated: curated list; optional live record check

steps.how: A text-generation service writes a short explanation from the verified results. It is automatically generated, has no human review, and is shown only if it passes checks for structure, unsupported numbers, links or citations, claims of safety or validation, and descriptions of how it was made. These checks test consistency, not scientific correctness. If it fails or is unavailable the assessment is shown without it.
steps.automated: automatically generated text, then code checks

steps.how: The status label, assumptions, missing information and limitations are produced by code from what was actually done.

notDone: No probability, severity, margin or confidence estimate.
No review by a qualified person or independent validation.

goals.label: Quick screening
goals.detail: Quick, 3 questions: the hazard plus three cabin-environment answers (gravity, oxygen, pressure), then your findings. Anything not asked is listed as information to add later.

goals.label: Investigate a specific hazard
goals.detail: Full, 20 to 29 questions in 5 to 7 short groups: Astroflare asks about the environment, the equipment and the safeguards, then reports conditions that warrant review in more detail.

goals.label: Find out what information is missing
goals.detail: A short path: only the hazard and the cabin environment are asked. Everything else is reported as missing, with why it matters.

goals.label: See which answers matter most
goals.detail: Full screening, then a check of how each answer you gave changes the findings and the heuristic index when varied.

unsupported.label: Radiation exposure
unsupported.message: Astroflare does not model radiation. Solar-flare records are shown only as context.

unsupported.label: Decompression or hull damage
unsupported.message: Astroflare does not model pressure loss or structural damage.

unsupported.label: Toxic or contaminated atmosphere (without a fire)
unsupported.message: Astroflare does not model atmospheric contamination. Its smoke path covers combustion products after a fire only.

unsupported.label: Propellant, engine or launch hazards
unsupported.message: Astroflare does not model propulsion, launch or entry hazards.

unsupported.label: Structural or mechanical failure
unsupported.message: Astroflare does not model mechanical failures.
